dosing_regimen.source_excerpt: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule.interventions and participant flow group descriptions: "Tralokinumab is a human recombinant monoclonal antibody of the immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) subclass that specifically binds to human interleukin (IL) 13 and blocks interaction with the IL-13 receptors." "Placebo contains the same excipients in the same concentration only lacking tralokinumab." "Subjects receiving initial treatment with tralokinumab 150 mg/tralokinumab 300 mg/placebo Q2W who did not achieve clinical response at Week 16 without use of rescue medication from Week 2 to Week 16, assigned to open-label treatment at Week 16 with tralokinumab 300 mg Q2W regimen + optional topical corticosteroids (TCS) OR Subjects receiving maintenance treatment with tralokinumab 150 mg Q2W/Q4W, tralokinumab 300 mg Q2W/Q4W, or placebo Q2W assigned to open-label treatment after Week 16 with tralokinumab 300 mg Q2W regimen + optional TCS if" "Initial Treatment Period - Tralokinumab 150 mg Q2W" "Tralokinumab 150 mg Q2W." "Tralokinumab: Tralokinumab is a human recombinant monoclonal antibody of the IgG4 subclass that specifically binds to human IL-13 and blocks interaction with the IL-13 receptors." "Tralokinumab (Dose1) initial-> Open-label tralokinumab" "Tralokinumab (Dose2) initial-> Open-label tralokinumab" "Tralokinumab(Dose1) initial-> Tralokinumab(Dose1) maintenanceA" "Tralokinumab(Dose1) initial-> Tralokinumab(Dose1) maintenanceB" "Tralokinumab(Dose2) initial-> Tralokinumab(Dose2) maintenanceA" "Tralokinumab(Dose2) initial-> Tralokinumab(Dose2) maintenanceB" "Placebo initial-> Open-label tralokinumab" -- Registry descriptions are copied verbatim. The registry includes dose 1 and dose 2 as separate groups (300 mg and 150 mg Q2W); one dose_value cannot represent both doses without selecting one, so it is null. Initial treatment is Q2W; maintenance can be Q2W or Q4W, so a single frequency is not assigned.

severity_criteria.source_excerpt: section 14 CLINICAL STUDIES, ECZTRA 6 description: "Pediatric Subjects 12 Years of Age and Older The efficacy of ADBRY monotherapy in pediatric subjects 12 years of age and older was assessed in a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (ECZTRA 6; NCT03526861) in 289 subjects 12 to 17 years of age with moderate-to-severe AD defined by IGA score ≥ 3 in the overall assessment of AD lesions on a severity scale of 0 to 4, an EASI score ≥ 16 at baseline, and a minimum BSA involvement of ≥10%." -- Label section 14 explicitly gives ECZTRA 6 baseline eligibility thresholds and calls disease moderate-to-severe.

value.population_note: The protocol describes the trial as tralokinumab monotherapy; subjects nevertheless had required background emollient treatment, permitted rescue treatment, and open-label TCS/TCI use. The enum has no monotherapy-with-emollient-and-rescue option, so regimen_type is null. Listed medication prohibitions apply during the periods stated by protocol.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: Sections 7.1 testing strategy and 14.3.4 multiple testing strategy: "The overall type I error rate in the tests of primary and secondary endpoints" "tested hierarchically at an overall 5% significance level, after which the" "significance level will be split evenly between testing of the same primary" "first be tested hierarchically at an overall 5% significance level, after which the significance" "level will be split evenly between:" "secondary endpoint Pruritus at Week 16 for the tralokinumab 300 mg dose in the US" "Dermatitis." "rejected, then the 2.5% significance level will be passed on to the testing of all the endpoints" "Unless otherwise stated, all significance tests will be 2-sided using the 5% significance level." "dose are rejected, then the 2.5% significance level will be passed on to the" "150 mg dose are rejected the 2.5% significance level will be passed on to the" "Note: To protect the family-wise type I error." "Note: To protect the family-wise type I error." "all the endpoints of the tralokinumab 150 mg dose are rejected, the 2.5% significance level" -- The protocol describes a graphical approach combining hierarchical co-primary testing and Holm–Bonferroni secondary-endpoint testing, with global (non-US) and US variants. After 300 mg testing, alpha is split evenly between 150 mg primary testing and 300 mg secondary testing; the exact named procedure has no single enum, so graphical is used for the stated graphical procedure and the variants are described here. A fixed endpoint order is not entered because the source says hierarchical testing but the typed sequence cannot preserve both regulatory branches. Alpha values are exact conversions of printed levels: 5% = 0.05 and 2.5% = 0.025.

value.rationale: Rescue treatment for intolerable AD symptoms is at investigator discretion; topical rescue continues with IMP, whereas systemic corticosteroid or non-steroidal systemic immunosuppressive rescue requires IMP discontinuation. Biological rescue is prohibited for the trial.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 9.5 Rescue treatment: "If medically necessary (i.e., to control intolerable AD symptoms), rescue treatment for AD" "may be provided to trial subjects at the discretion of the investigator." "Subjects who receive topical rescue treatment (TCS of any WHO class [see Appendix 6], or" "TCI) will continue treatment with IMP." "adequately after at least 14 days of topical treatment." "If a subject receives rescue treatment with systemic corticosteroids or non-steroidal systemic" "etc.), IMP will be immediately discontinued (see Section 10.2.2, reasons for temporary" "be resumed if deemed appropriate by the investigator, but not sooner than 5 half-lives after the" "The use of biological rescue treatment will be" "However, systemic rescue treatment" "Investigators should make every attempt to conduct efficacy and safety assessments (at least" "will be transferred to open-label treatment, but not sooner than 5 half-lives after the last dose" "safety follow-up (Week 66) must be recorded in the subject’s medical record and the eCRF" -- Rescue for intolerable AD symptoms may be provided at investigator discretion. The protocol says to attempt topical treatment first and escalate after at least 14 days if inadequate, but permits immediate systemic rescue when appropriate, so the fixed topical minimum-days field is left null. Biological rescue is disallowed for the entire trial.
